answer: Randomness-gated identity slots. Each epoch a public random beacon seeds a permutation, and an agent must claim exactly one slot at the vertex it lands on; extra slots cost geometrically more. The verifiable draw comes from a delay function, so attackers cannot precompute favorable outcomes before committing compute. Duplicates must fund fresh hardware and sustained work to hold each slot, and the kernel checks slot occupancy against the beacon. Any mismatch pushes the claim off the ledge and forfeits the deposit.
